blocks.text: Queen Mary Park home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

44 townhomes sold in Queen Mary Park with a median price of $669,000 (the middle half sold between $614,975 and $725,750), taking a median of 38 days to sell at 97.1% of the last list price; 14% sold above list. They had a median $455 per square foot, a median year built of 1988 and a median strata fee of $351 a month. 36 condos sold in Queen Mary Park with a median price of $436,500 (the middle half sold between $367,500 and $530,500), taking a median of 44 days to sell at 96.3% of the last list price; 3% sold above list. They had a median $513 per square foot, a median year built of 1996 and a median strata fee of $416 a month.

By Whitetail Homes. By Whitetail Homes, the companion building to Galilea on the same 94A Avenue/95 Avenue ground. A project source states six storeys and 125 condominiums over two levels of underground parking, with completion estimated for spring 2026; current listings record it built 2026, Apartment/Condo, subdivision Gabriel, and describe units as move-in ready, and the building directory records Gabriel Condos built 2026. A listing header records "Cats OK."
UNCONFIRMED, not counted — "Celest," said to be at 8183 121A Street
The building is therefore documented as an unnamed, uncounted building at 8183 121A Street until a directory, developer or City source confirms the name.
Another index-page address, 10721 139 Street, has no verified building name and sits at the Whalley edge — UNCONFIRMED, not counted.

items.t: Queen Mary Park Surrey is a board sub-area in central Surrey, west of King George Boulevard and south of 96 Avenue, named for the City park of the same name. It has no City of Surrey neighbourhood or plan-area boundary — the City does not plan it as a named neighbourhood — so its formal boundaries are UNVERIFIED, and no boundary line for it should be published as fact.
That is a listing observation from one reading, not a boundary.

The sub-area sits where two City communities meet — Whalley/City Centre to the north and Newton to the south — and which City community a specific address falls in is address-specific and UNVERIFIED at the area level.

Queen Mary Park itself is at 8972 Queen Mary Boulevard, north of 88 Avenue and west of 132 Street: natural trails loop the northwest portion, with a playground and the Healy Creek ecosystem. The City's park page does not list gardens, picnic areas or sports facilities for this park — wider descriptions circulating in site copy are not City facts. Bear Creek Park (13750 88 Avenue) is at the sub-area's northeast and Queen Elizabeth Meadows Park is at 9400 134 Street.

Transit frames both edges: the R1 King George Boulevard RapidBus runs along the east side and the R6 Scott Road RapidBus along Scott Road (120 Street) on the west side, both connecting to Expo Line stations — which is why the sub-area's condo clusters sit at its two edges, on 120A/121A Streets in the south and on 134 Street in the north. The planned King George Boulevard BRT would also run along the east edge.
Surrey Memorial Hospital stands at 13750 96 Avenue on the sub-area's north edge, and the Surrey-Newton Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 6830 King George Boulevard on the east side.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Queen Mary Park Surrey

items.t: The Form B Information Certificate is the buyer's core document in every Queen Mary Park strata: under s. 59 of the Strata Property Act the strata must provide it within 7 days of a request, for a fee of no more than $35 plus up to 25 cents per page for copies. It carries the unit's fee, the CRF balance, parking and storage allocation, and the bylaws actually in force.
In the 1990s southern cluster this report is the key document: it is where a claim like Sterling Court's "completely rainscreened, new building envelope" is either documented or not.
Minimum CRF contribution: since November 1, 2023, stratas must contribute at least 10% of the annual operating fund to the contingency reserve fund each year.
Rentals: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022.
Age bylaws: the only age-restriction bylaw a BC strata may enforce is 55+, under ss. 123.1 and 123.2 of the Strata Property Act, with exemptions added May 1, 2023.
Pets: pet limits remain lawful strata bylaws.

Zoning and plan status: Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 governs, under the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026). Queen Mary Park has no neighbourhood plan of its own, so there is no NCP designation sheet to quote for these buildings — any source presenting one is presenting something that does not exist.

Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) and suites: Surrey permits 3 units on lots under 280 m² and 4 units on lots over 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of 281 m² or more within 400 m of a frequent bus stop — both RapidBus edges (R1 and R6) put much of this sub-area's house stock inside a frequent-stop band. One secondary suite per house is permitted under the BC Building Code framework, and an unpermitted suite is not made legal by the SSMUH rules. That matters here because the sub-area's house listings openly describe unauthorized suites; the legality of any specific suite is per-property and UNCONFIRMED until the permits are checked.
Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty applied after July 2 and a further 5% after September 2.

GST on new builds is 5%. It does not apply to ordinary resales — a Quinn resale listing says so for its own unit — but it does apply to developer sales, which is the live question at Gabriel (completed 2026) and any developer-held units at Galilea and Quinn. The first-time home buyers' GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026, per CRA Excise and GST/HST News No. 122) rebates 100% of the GST on a new home priced up to $1M (maximum $50,000), phasing out to $1.5M, for agreements entered into from March 20, 2025 to 2031. The older GST New Housing Rebate covers homes the FTHB rebate does not: 36% of the GST, maximum $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000.

BC Property Transfer Tax: 1% on the first $200,000, 2% on the portion up to $2M, 3% above $2M, plus a further 2% on the residential portion of a price above $3M. The First-Time Home Buyers' exemption is full up to $835,000 fair market value (on the first $500,000) and partial up to $860,000; the Newly Built Home Exemption is full up to $1.1M and partial up to $1.15M — the exemption that matters for a developer purchase at Gabriel or Galilea.

Federal first-time buyer tools: the Home Buyers' Plan allows a $60,000 RRSP withdrawal; the First Home Savings Account allows $40,000 lifetime at $8,000 per year. CMHC mortgage insurance premiums run 0.6%–4.5%.

Presales and new completions: REDMA gives a 7-day rescission period under s. 21 and requires purchase deposits to be held in trust under s. 18 — the framework for developer contracts at Gabriel and any remaining developer inventory at Galilea and Quinn.

blocks.text: Good to know about Queen Mary Park Surrey

items.t: The neighbourhood is named for a park most listings over-describe: the City's own page for Queen Mary Park lists trails, a playground and the Healy Creek ecosystem — and does not list the gardens, picnic areas or sports facilities that appear in marketing copy for the area.

One building in the southern cluster cannot be honestly named in these notes: the condo building at 8183 121A Street is real (a current listing index confirms the address and type), but its name, storeys and build year exist only on a source these notes do not cite — so it is carried as UNCONFIRMED and uncounted rather than named on a single weak source.

Eclipse is the opposite case — a name with a paper trail: Surrey Council minutes from 2006 and 2007 record the four-storey apartment building approved at 8084 120A Street, so the building's existence and form rest on a City primary source even though its build year and unit count stay UNCONFIRMED.

The northern cluster is a two-developer story: Porte built Quinn (174 units, 2024), and Whitetail built Galilea (129 homes) and Gabriel (125 condos) side by side on the same 94A/95 Avenue ground — Galilea's sales centre served both projects, so early Gabriel buyers were sold from inside Galilea.

Quinn's own directory presence contains a trap: a "22-unit development" header attached to its 9456 134 Street address contradicts the project's documented 174 units — a per-page directory figure that should never be quoted as the building's size.
The two halves of this small sub-area do not behave alike.

There is no Queen Mary Park Elementary anchoring this neighbourhood in the research record — the name comes from the City park, and the elementary schools on the Ministry list for this ground are David Brankin, Senator Reid, Betty Huff, Kennedy Trail and Kirkbride. Any source that names a "Queen Mary Park Elementary" as the local school is asserting something this research could not verify.

items.t: Queen Mary Park is a Fraser Valley board sub-area in central Surrey, west of King George Boulevard and south of 96 Avenue, named for Queen Mary Park, the City park at 8972 Queen Mary Blvd, Surrey. Formal boundaries: UNVERIFIED — no City neighbourhood or plan-area boundary for "Queen Mary Park" as a residential area was confirmed on an official source; the live feed's span at reading (Scott Road / 120 Street east to 134 Street, 81 Avenue north to 96 Avenue, 167 results) is a listing observation, not a boundary.

The City park page places the park north of 88 Avenue and west of 132 Street and lists natural trails looping through its northwest portion, a playground, and the Healy Creek ecosystem; it does not list gardens, picnic areas or sports facilities — the live page's wider amenity description is site copy, not a City fact.

The sub-area sits at the meeting of the City-published Whalley / City Centre side (north) and Newton side (south); which City community a specific address falls in is address-specific: UNVERIFIED as an area-wide statement.
Surrey community medians (sub-area medians are not published: UNVERIFIED at sub-area level): detached $1,215,000; attached $512,944, $491/sq ft, 99% sale-to-list, 25 days on market.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: two pockets — the 121A Street cluster south of 84 Avenue around Scott Road (Hadley Green, Lakewood Grove, Kennedy Woods, Kennedy Trail, Barkerville II), and the 122 Street cluster south of 96 Avenue (Bonnydoon Village, Whispering Cedars).

Matheson Secondary, 9484 122 St. Catchments are address-based through the SD36 School Locator; no locator run for a Queen Mary Park address is on record, so the catchment school for any specific address is UNVERIFIED.

Transit: the R1 King George Blvd RapidBus runs on King George Boulevard at the east side and the R6 Scott Road RapidBus runs on Scott Road (120 Street) at the west side, both connecting to Expo Line stations; TransLink is advancing King George Boulevard BRT (approximately 19 km, 12 stations, now in full design) along the eastern edge.
Health care: Surrey Memorial Hospital, 13750 96 Ave, sits at the sub-area's north edge; the Surrey-Newton Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 6830 King George Blvd.

items.t: Form B diligence (all 7 strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.

blocks.text: Good to know about Queen Mary Park

items.t: The park the area is named for is smaller in the City's telling than in listing copy. The City's Queen Mary Park page lists trails, a playground and the Healy Creek ecosystem at 8972 Queen Mary Blvd — and does not list the gardens, picnic areas or sports facilities the live page's editorial describes.

Two "Lakewood" names, two different sub-areas, opposite age rules. Lakewood Grove (8257 121A St, this sub-area) shows no age restriction in any source checked, while Lakewood Place and Lakewood Heights on W Boundary Drive (Panorama Ridge) are verified 55+ townhouses. A name-based alert mixes them.
The sub-area's detached market was the quietest in Surrey in September 2026.

The townhouse stock is old, and that is the diligence story. Five of the seven counted complexes date from 1974–1991 on their verified records (Bonnydoon Village 1974, Barkerville II 1988, Hadley Green 1989, Lakewood Grove 1991, Kennedy Trail 2008 the exception) — depreciation reports and CRF balances matter more here than in Surrey's newer townhouse pockets.

No City plan area stands behind the name. "Queen Mary Park" is a board sub-area and a park name, not a City planning district — City documents for this ground are filed under Whalley / City Centre and Newton framings, so a search run under only the board name misses them.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Queen Mary Park?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 89 condos and townhomes listed in Queen Mary Park. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Queen Mary Park a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Queen Mary Park had a sales ratio of 9%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Queen Mary Park from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 37 condos and townhomes sold in Queen Mary Park over those 4 months, out of 591 in all of Surrey.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did townhomes in Queen Mary Park sell for?
faq.a: 44 townhomes sold in Queen Mary Park between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $669,000.

faq.q: How long do townhomes take to sell in Queen Mary Park?
faq.a: The median was 38 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.1% of the last list price (14% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: How many townhouse complexes are verified in Queen Mary Park?
faq.a: Seven, all strata: Lakewood Grove, Kennedy Woods, Kennedy Trail, Hadley Green and Barkerville II on 121A Street, plus Bonnydoon Village and Whispering Cedars on 122 Street.

faq.q: Is there a Queen Mary Park Elementary for my kids?
faq.a: No such school exists — the name was invented from a park name in other copy. The Ministry-listed elementaries for this ground are David Brankin, Senator Reid, Betty Huff, Kennedy Trail and Kirkbride; catchments are address-based in SD36 and no locator run for a Queen Mary Park address is on record, so run the exact address in the SD36 School Locator.

faq.q: Can I rent out my Queen Mary Park townhouse?
faq.a: Long-term, yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022.

faq.q: Are Bakersville and Barkerville II the same complex?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED. Do not merge them on a spelling guess — the Form B and strata plan for the specific unit settle it.

faq.q: What should I worry about in Bonnydoon Village (1974) or Whispering Cedars?
faq.a: Levies and the depreciation report. Every strata of five or more lots must renew its report every five years since July 1, 2024; at 50 years old, envelope, roofing and plumbing items dominate. Whispering Cedars' build year itself is UNCONFIRMED in citable sources — another reason the strata documents, not listing copy, carry the diligence.
